dedupe_keys.name: parkserve u s park boundaries and 10 minute walk service areas

description: ParkServe is the Trust for Public Land's database of publicly accessible parks in every U.S. urban area, with about 148,000 parks, most added from 2016 to 2018 by requesting data from each city or town. It holds park boundary polygons and attributes, places and urban areas following Census Bureau definitions, and a 10-minute walk service area for every park, built on Esri's walkable road network with barriers such as highways, railways and unbridged rivers, from auto-generated or, for the 100 ParkScore cities, verified access points. Access statistics are broken down by race and ethnicity, age and income using Esri demographic estimates, and the guide explains park prioritisation and custom analyses. Coverage: U.S. urban areas; the 100 most populous cities are updated each year with park agencies and treated as complete. Access: downloads and ArcGIS services. Licence: TPL terms, not read. Caveats: outside the 100 cities data are mostly as of 2018, and demographics depend on licensed Esri estimates. Simulation uses: park access and equity analysis, heat refuge planning and siting new parks. Related records: OpenStreetMap parks and OS Open Greenspace.
